Choose an action by expected utility, with grounding and abstention

Source: R/decide.R
decide.Rd

The shared decision rule. Given draws from the posterior of a latent state \(\theta\), a utility function \(U(a, \theta)\), and a set of candidate actions, decide() evaluates the expected utility \(E_\theta[U(a, \theta)]\) of each feasible candidate by averaging over the draws and selects the maximiser. It declines to do so – abstaining to safe_action – under any of four conditions, checked in this order: the combined input grounding is not grounded (the Independent Oracle Principle firewall: never act on an unverified fact); no candidate satisfies constraint; the effective sample size is below min_ess (this trigger is opt-in – it never fires unless the caller supplies min_ess, since there is no universal floor a decision-agnostic engine can default to); or the chosen action beats the safe_action on fewer than decisive_prob of the draws (it is not clearly better than the status quo). The last check is judged against the safe action, not the runner-up, so a fine candidate grid does not trigger spurious indecision; when safe_action has no numeric match in candidates (a categorical action set, or an off-grid numeric safe action) it falls back to the per-draw argmax probability, so the gate stays live for every candidate shape rather than becoming a no-op.

Usage

decide(
  draws,
  utility,
  candidates,
  labels = NULL,
  constraint = NULL,
  grounding = grounding_unverified(),
  safe_action = NULL,
  safe_label = "abstain",
  min_ess = NULL,
  ess = NULL,
  decisive_prob = 0.6,
  method = "expected_utility",
  inputs = list(),
  metadata = list()
)

Arguments

draws

A numeric vector of posterior draws of the latent state.

utility

A function function(action, theta) returning a numeric vector of utilities the same length as theta.

candidates

A numeric vector (or list) of candidate actions.

labels

Optional character labels for the candidates; defaults to a formatted candidates.

constraint

Optional function(action) returning TRUE when the action is feasible.

grounding

One or more grounding tokens for the inputs; combined worst-case.

safe_action

The action returned on abstention (e.g. a flat position, a zero input rate, the status quo).

safe_label

A label for the safe action.

min_ess

Optional effective-sample-size floor; the low_ess abstention trigger is off by default and fires only when this is set.

ess

Optional effective sample size of draws; defaults to length(draws).

decisive_prob

The minimum posterior probability that the chosen action beats safe_action, below which the decision abstains as not clearly better than the status quo.

method

A label recording the decision rule.

inputs

A named list recording input provenance.

metadata

A named list of free-form metadata.

Value

A decision object.

Details

The grounding label is combined worst-case across grounding with combine_grounding(), so passing the provenance of several inputs taints the decision if any one of them is unverified.

See also

decide_input_rate() and decide_position_size() for domain wrappers; decision for the returned object.

Other decisions: decide_input_rate(), decide_position_size(), decision(), is_grounded()

Examples

set.seed(1L)
theta <- rnorm(2000L, mean = 1.2, sd = 0.4)
u <- function(a, theta) -(a - theta)^2
decide(theta, u, candidates = seq(0, 3, by = 0.5),
       grounding = grounding_grounded(), safe_action = 0)
#> <decision> decided  [grounded]
#>   action : 1
#>   E[utility]: -0.2098
#>   candidates: 7 evaluated (method: expected_utility)
